planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in fall in moist, humus-rich woodland soil in light to partial shade, siting it where the climbing stems can lean on neighboring shrubs or a support.

directions: 'Bellagio' is a free-offsetting selection of the Chinese climbing Solomon's seal, forming a thick dormant rhizome that sends up sturdy round stalks each spring lined with whorled, narrow leaves ending in curling, tendril-like tips. In late spring the leaf axils carry clusters of bell-shaped orange flowers with contrasting chartreuse tips, a showier and more floriferous display than the typical species. Unlike many Polygonatum, this selection thickens into a multi-stemmed clump fairly quickly and benefits from the support of nearby shrubs or a trellis as stems lengthen with age. Give it rich, well-drained woodland soil and consistent moisture during the growing season for the best flowering display.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade, where the dark emerging stems can be appreciated against lighter companions.

directions: 'Shina no Tsuki' (sold in the trade as China Moon) is a Japanese-origin selection of this Chinese fairy bells valued for its distinctly dark, near-black new stems and foliage as they emerge in spring before mellowing toward green with maturity. Clusters of small, pendant, creamy-white bell flowers dangle beneath the whorled leaves in spring, followed later by dark berries. It forms a slowly expanding clump of arching, bamboo-like stems well suited to a shaded woodland bed where the contrast of its dark new growth against ferns and hostas can be enjoyed up close. Divide congested clumps in early spring to maintain vigor and share increase.

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring or fall and plant horizontally in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in shade; mark the spot as it emerges late.

directions: 'Ramosissima' is an RHS-recognized selection of common Solomon's seal distinguished from the typical unbranched species by its freely branching, spreading habit, with slightly arching stems that fork repeatedly rather than rising as single unbranched wands. Small axillary clusters of nodding, tubular, creamy-white flowers tipped in green appear in late spring along the branched stems, followed by black berries in autumn. The denser, more twiggy branching gives established plants a fuller, bushier silhouette than the species, useful where a slightly more substantial architectural mass is wanted in the woodland border. Grow and divide it exactly as for the species, in moist, humus-rich shaded soil, dividing congested clumps in spring or fall.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade, where its pale foliage will show up best against darker companions.

directions: 'Snow Stream' is a variegated selection of Japanese fairy bells with distinctively wavy, undulating leaves whose centers are washed in white and edged in a contrasting band of dark green, giving a more irregular, streaked look than the plain-margined 'Variegatum'. Small, creamy-white, bell-shaped flowers dangle from the leaf axils in early spring before the foliage fully expands. It spreads gradually by rhizome into a low, slow-creeping patch, making it a good choice for a shaded rock garden edge or container where the bright foliage can be viewed closely. Keep soil consistently moist and humus-rich, and divide clumps in spring if growth becomes congested.
